inbox.title: Notes on a quieter inbox
inbox.author: robin
inbox.excerpt: For a month I only opened notifications twice a day. Here's what changed, and what I'd keep.
body: For a month I only opened notifications twice a day: once with coffee, once before signing off. Everything else waited.
The surprise wasn't how much I missed. It was how little. Most things that felt urgent at 10am were already answered by noon.
What I'd keep: skim first, read second. If a headline and two lines don't earn a click, the post can wait for the weekend.

comments.text: Love this. The bit about batching replies changed my mornings already.
Glad it helped! Coffee and notifications is a strong combo.
Do you keep the browser closed the rest of the day? That's where I slip.
Same question. My tabs are a crime scene.

crit.title: Design crit, week 42
crit.author: theo
crit.excerpt: Agenda for Thursday: onboarding illustrations, the new empty states, and menu bar sketches.
body: Agenda for Thursday's crit, in order:
1. Onboarding illustrations, final pass. 2. Empty states for search and saved items.
3. @robin can you share the menu bar sketches before Thursday? Rough is fine. We mostly want to talk about density.

comments.text: I'll bring the empty states. Two directions, one weird.

sourdough.title: Sourdough, but lazier
sourdough.author: jules
sourdough.excerpt: No stretch-and-folds, no schedule. A loaf that forgives you for forgetting about it.
body: Every sourdough recipe wants you home all day. This one doesn't. Mix, leave it in the fridge, forget about it for two days.
The long cold rest does the work you'd normally do by hand. You lose a little height and gain a lot of flavor.
Bake it in a hot pot with the lid on for twenty minutes, then lid off until it's darker than you think it should be.

comments.text: Made it this weekend. My kitchen smells like a bakery and I did nothing.
Does it work with whole wheat?
Yes! Add a splash more water.

waits.title: The case for software that waits
waits.author: kofi
waits.excerpt: Not every update needs a badge. Some of the best tools just wait until you come back.
body: Not every update needs a badge. The tools I keep longest are the ones that wait patiently until I come back.
Waiting is a design choice. It says: you decide when this matters. The opposite is a slot machine with a settings page.
Try it for a week: turn the badges off and check in on your own schedule. You can always turn them back on.

comments.text: Badges off is the best productivity tip nobody wants to hear.

scopes.title: Seven small telescopes, ranked
scopes.author: lena
scopes.excerpt: Under 3kg, under $500, and all of them will show you Saturn's rings from a balcony.
body: Every one of these fits in a backpack, sets up in under five minutes, and will show you Saturn's rings from a city balcony.
The winner isn't the sharpest. It's the one you'll actually carry outside on a weeknight.

train.title: Release train 4.2 is boarding
train.author: sam
train.excerpt: Code freeze Friday. Release notes due Monday. Here's the checklist.
body: Code freeze is Friday at noon. Anything not merged by then rides the next train, no hard feelings.
Release notes are due Monday. If your change is user-visible, a single plain sentence is perfect.

comments.text: Notes for the offline mode fix are in the doc.

focaccia.title: Weeknight focaccia
focaccia.author: jules
focaccia.excerpt: Stir it at breakfast, bake it at dinner. The fridge does the rest.
body: Stir flour, water, salt and yeast together at breakfast. Cover it and put it in the fridge.
At dinner, tip it into an oiled pan, poke it all over and bake it hot until the top is deep gold.

comments.text: Rosemary and flaky salt. That's the whole review.

material.title: Notifications are a design material
material.author: kofi
material.excerpt: Every ping is a decision someone made about your attention. We can make better ones.
body: Every ping is a decision someone made about your attention, usually without asking you.
Treat notifications like any other material: choose them on purpose, and use as few as you can.
